description: helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests keeps the digest pinning in .github/workflows self-enforcing. Every `uses:` there is pinned to a commit SHA with the tag kept in a trailing comment; without this preset a newly added action written as `@v1` would silently stay unpinned and the sweep would decay one workflow at a time. It ships in config:best-practices rather than config:recommended, so it has to be listed here.

minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour: timestamp-optional is what stops those digest pins from freezing. minimumReleaseAge applies to digest updates too, and when Renovate cannot date one it treats it as pending forever under the default timestamp-required — which is exactly the case for a ref that is not a version, such as pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1. timestamp-optional keeps the 14-day delay wherever a release timestamp exists and lets the undatable updates through instead of stalling them indefinitely.

packageRules.description: Replacement and pin updates carry no release timestamp, so the release-age check can never be satisfied and would leave renovate/stability-days pending forever. security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm exempts these for npm; we do the same for all datasources. lockFileMaintenance is exempted in its own config block below.

Hold TypeScript inside typescript-eslint's peer range, which is `>=4.8.4 <6.1.0` (seven packages in pnpm-lock.yaml declare it). typescript-eslint reaches us transitively via @nuxt/eslint -> @nuxt/eslint-config, so we cannot bump it independently; forcing TS7 crashes eslint with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'Cjs')". The bound is <6.1 rather than <7 so it tracks the peer range itself instead of merely excluding the next major -- TS 6.1 would violate the peer range too. This rule only constrains what renovate proposes, so the devDependency is `~6.0.3` rather than `^6.0.3`; otherwise lockFileMaintenance would resolve 6.1 inside the caret range and bypass this entirely. Lift the bound and widen the range together once typescript-eslint widens its peer: `npm view typescript-eslint peerDependencies`.

customManagers.description: jdx/mise-action's `version:` input pins the mise CLI that CI runs, so a workflow resolves tools with the same mise as local development instead of whatever released last night. Renovate's github-actions manager only updates `uses:` refs and reads no action inputs, so without this manager the pin would rot silently. The marker comment is what makes the match robust: keying off the `version:` line alone would also catch every other action's `version:` input. mise tags releases as `vYYYY.M.PATCH`; extractVersionTemplate drops the leading `v` to match the bare version the input expects.
